learning_objective: 🎯 Become a responsible digital citizen by learning about online safety, netiquette, and protecting intellectual property rights in the digital world.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: साहित्यिक चोरी (दूसरों का काम कॉपी करना)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Just like we have manners in real life, we need manners online. Netiquette means being respectful, not using ALL CAPS (which implies shouting), not spreading rumors, and respecting others' privacy.

Everything you do online—searches, social media posts, comments—leaves a trail. This is your digital footprint. It is permanent, and future employers or colleges can see it. Always think before you post!
When someone creates original work (software, music, art), they own it. Copying someone's work without permission is Plagiarism. IPR is protected through Copyrights, Patents, and Trademarks.

Proprietary software (like MS Word) is owned by a company, costs money, and you can't see its source code. Open Source Software (like Linux or Python) is free, and anyone can view, edit, and share its code.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Google Yourself
fun_activity.instructions: Type your full name in quotation marks (e.g., "Rohan Sharma") into Google Search. See what comes up! The images and links you see are part of your 'Digital Footprint'. Are you happy with what the internet knows about you?

exam_tips: 📌 Always define Plagiarism as 'stealing someone else's intellectual work and passing it off as your own without giving credit'.
📌 Cyberbullying includes sending threatening messages, posting embarrassing photos, or creating fake profiles to harass someone.
📌 FOSS stands for Free and Open Source Software. 'Free' means freedom to modify, not just free of cost.
quick_recap: ⭐ Phishing is a cybercrime where attackers trick you into giving passwords by pretending to be a trusted entity (like a bank).
⭐ E-commerce safety involves checking for 'https' (the 's' stands for secure) and a padlock symbol before entering payment details.
⭐ Software licenses define how you can legally use, modify, or distribute a piece of software.
